data.title: Message Queue
data.tagline: A communication and decoupling mechanism that temporarily stores messages between senders and receivers so neither must wait synchronously.
data.learningOutcome: You can identify the API, queue, and worker roles, then use one job ID to distinguish queued, processing, completed, and failed states.
data.description: When a user exports a large report, the API creates a job, writes its ID and parameters to a queue, and immediately returns a pending status. A worker generates the file and updates the same ID to completed or failed. Enqueueing proves receipt, not completion, and retries can cause the same job to be delivered again.

learning.assumes: You have seen pages that say 'Processing, check back later' after submitting a heavy task.
learning.outcome: You can identify the API, queue, and worker roles, then use one job ID to distinguish queued, processing, completed, and failed states.

distinctions.label: Enqueue Operation
distinctions.explanation: A Message Queue is the infrastructure that buffers and routes messages; Enqueue is the single operation of putting a message into that queue.

distinctions.label: Consumer
distinctions.explanation: A Message Queue holds pending work; a Message Consumer is the worker process that reads messages from the queue and executes business logic.

explanation.title: Before: the page waits for all background work
explanation.text: After the user clicks Export, one request queries data, builds the file, and uploads it. A slow step can leave the page spinning or time out, and the user has no durable task status to check later.

explanation.title: Enqueue the work and return status through one task ID
explanation.text: The API creates export_104, enqueues its parameters and ID, and returns that ID. A worker marks the same task processing, then stores either a file location or readable failure. The page shows queued, processing, completed, or failed under that ID. Enqueued means accepted, not completed.

explanation.title: Verify evidence across the whole path
explanation.text: Match export_104 across the API response, queued message, worker log, and final UI state. Retry a failed task and confirm duplicate delivery does not create two files. A single 'message enqueued' log does not prove completion.

data.boundary: Ordering and delivery count depend on the queue and its configuration. Reliable systems often redeliver unacknowledged messages, so a worker must handle duplicates and record failures, retries, and final state. Product-specific configuration is outside this introduction.

lessonPractice.title: After paying for an order, SMS confirmation and invoicing are needed. What is the primary benefit of using a message queue?

options.label: After payment completes, the API enqueues SMS and invoicing tasks, returns the order result, and lets workers process them
options.feedback: Correct. The tasks no longer occupy the payment request, while workers still need failure, retry, and final-state handling.

options.label: The checkout API must block until the queue confirms that both SMS delivery and invoice generation have succeeded
options.feedback: Incorrect. That remains synchronous blocking and defeats the purpose of async queueing.

options.label: Once a task enters the message queue, the SMS is considered delivered without requiring any worker to process it
options.feedback: Incorrect. Enqueueing only stores the job; a background consumer must still execute it.

data.agentPrompt: This Excel export blocks the request too long. Make it asynchronous: create and enqueue a job, return its ID immediately, and have the worker update queued, processing, completed, or failed under the same ID. Make duplicate delivery safe, then verify both a successful export and a worker failure.
